rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is coordinated with illness and covers journeys of any length; this wording is clearer than simply saying “travelers.”
rows.anchor: عطف على مرضى أي أو كنتم على سفر ما طال أو قصر

rows.speaker: الهداية
rows.claim: Al-Hidaya allows tayammum for someone without water who is traveling or at least a mile outside town.
rows.anchor: ومن لم يجد الماء وهو مسافر أو خارج المصر بينه وبين المصر ميل أو أكثر يتيمم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For a nontraveling person outside town, the same rule follows by analogy, not directly from the text.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن حكم من هو خارج المصر غير مسافر كما يقتضيه العطف معلوم بالقياس لا بالنص

rows.speaker: من حمل الصلاة على مواضعها
rows.claim: One parsing takes prayer as its locations and crossing as passing through them, so the later condition states a distinct rule.
rows.anchor: من حمل الصلاة على مواضعها وفسر العبور بالاجتياز بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The recommended pause after “until you wash” and the spatial language of approaching, crossing, and travel support that interpretation.
rows.anchor: القراء كلهم استحبوا الوقف عند قوله سبحانه : ( حتى تغتسلوا )

rows.speaker: الكثير
rows.claim: Many commentators take the passage otherwise than the spatial interpretation of prayer and crossing.
rows.anchor: إلا أن الكثير على خلافه وإنما قدم المرض على السفر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Travel is mentioned to connect illness with travel and equate them through inability to use water, even when water is present.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ذكر السفر هنا لإلحاق المرض به والتسوية بينه وبينه بإلحاق الواجد بالفاقد بجامع العجز عن الاستعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Illness precedes travel to signal its primacy and independent rulings, which do not occur in other cases.
rows.anchor: وإنما قدم المرض على السفر للإيذان بأصالته واستقلاله بأحكام لا توجد في غيره

rows.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
rows.claim: Ibrahim al-Nakha'i reports that wounded Companions developed widespread injuries, then janaba, complained to the Prophet, and the illness clause was revealed.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن جريج عن إبراهيم النخعي قال : نال أصحاب النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم جراحة

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority report revelation at al-Muraysiʿ: ʿAisha lost Asma's necklace during travel, the party lacked water, and tayammum was revealed; Usayd praised the blessing and relief granted to Aisha's family.
rows.anchor: هذا خلاف ما عليه الجمهور حيث رووا أن نزولها في غزوة المريسيع حين عرس رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ghaʾiṭ originally means a low place; going there became a euphemism for relieving oneself because people concealed themselves from view.
rows.anchor: وهو المكان المنخفض وجاء الغيط بفتح الغين وسكون الياء

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud reads al-ghayṭ with fatḥa on ghayn and a still yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وبه قرأ ابن مسعود رضي الله تعالى عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One derivation treats ghayṭ as the verbal noun of yaghūṭ, with the expected wāw changed to yāʾ and made still.
rows.anchor: وهو في رأي مصدر يغوط وكان القياس غوطا فقلبت الواو ياءا وسكنت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preferable account treats ghayṭ as a lightened form, like the variant pair hayyin and hayyin.
rows.anchor: ولعل الأولى ما قيل : إنه تخفيف غيط كهين وهين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular “someone” hints that people go alone when relieving themselves, as custom and proper conduct require.
rows.anchor: وفي ذكر ( أحد ) فيه دون غيره إيماء إلى أن الإنسان ينفرد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation says the singular subject avoids explicitly attributing an embarrassing or disagreeable act to the audience.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إنما ذكر وأسند المجئ إليه دون المخاطبين تفاديا عن التصريح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause is coordinated with “you were”; the first prepositional phrase describes the preceding indefinite, and the second attaches to the verb.
rows.anchor: والفعل عطف على ( كنتم ) والجار الأول متعلق بمحذوف وقع صفة للنكرة قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Touching women” euphemistically means intercourse, indicating major impurity, while the preceding clause indicates minor impurity.
rows.anchor: يريد سبحانه أو جامعتم النساء إلا أنه كنى بالملامسة عن الجماع

rows.speaker: علي وابن عباس والحسن
rows.claim: ʿAli, Ibn ʿAbbas, and al-Hasan are cited for the intercourse reading, which indicates major impurity.
rows.anchor: وإلى ذلك ذهب علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه وابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما والحسن

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود والنخعي والشعبي
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud, al-Nakhaʿi, and al-Shaʿbi interpret the phrase as skin touching short of intercourse.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود والنخعي والشعبي أن المراد بالملامسة ما دون الجماع

rows.speaker: الشافعي والزهري والأوزاعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafiʿi infers that touching a woman invalidates ablution; al-Zuhri and al-Awzaʿi agree.
rows.anchor: وبه استدل الشافعي رضي الله تعالى عنه على أن اللمس ينقض الوضوء وبه قال الزهري والأوزاعي

rows.speaker: مالك والليث بن سعد وأحمد
rows.claim: Malik, al-Layth, and one report from Ahmad say touching invalidates ablution only when accompanied by desire.
rows.anchor: وقال مالك والليث بن سعد وأحمد في إحدى الروايات عنه : إن كان اللمس بشهوة نقض وإلا فلا

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa holds that touching does not invalidate ablution, even with desire; another qualification says it does if erection occurs.
rows.anchor: وذهب أبو حنيفة رضي الله تعالى عنه إلى أنه لا ينتقض الوضوء بالمس ولو بشهوة قيل : ما لم يحدث الإنتشار

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafiʿi differed over touching close relatives or a young unrelated woman; his sounder view is that it does not invalidate ablution, like touching teeth, nails, or hair.
rows.anchor: واختلف قول الشافعي رضي الله تعالى عنه في لمس المحارم كالأم والبنت والأخت وفي لمس الأجنبية الصغيرة وأصح القولين : إنه لا ينقض

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: In al-Shafiʿi's stronger view, the person touched also loses ablution because both participants share the possibility of pleasure, as in intercourse.
rows.anchor: وينتقض عنده وضوء الملموسة كاللامس في الأظهر لاشتراكهما في مظنة اللذة كالمشتركين في الجماع

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafiʿi does not invalidate the touched person's ablution when their private part is touched, since that person did not touch a locus of pleasure.
rows.anchor: وإنما لم ينتقض وضوء الملموس فرجه على مذهبه لأنه لم يوجد منه مس لمظنة لذة أصلا

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha reports placing her hand on the Prophet's feet while he prostrated, evidence cited against invalidating ablution for the person touched.
rows.anchor: حديث عائشة رضي الله تعالى عنها أنها وضعت يدها على قدميه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The literal sense is stronger, especially in Hamza and al-Kisaʾi's reading aw lamastum, since لمس is less established as a euphemism for intercourse than ملامسة.
rows.anchor: أن الحمل على الحقيقة هو الراجح لا سيما في قراءة حمزة والكسائي أو لمستم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Others prefer interpreting both readings as intercourse, privileging figurative usage and reconciling the readings; this matches the Hanafi position.
rows.anchor: ورجح بعضهم الحمل على الجماع في القراءتين ترجيحا للمجاز والمشهور

rows.speaker: بعض المحققين
rows.claim: Some investigators say mutual bodily contact by any body part is the literal meaning, which includes intercourse; it is metaphor only when intercourse alone is intended.
rows.anchor: إن الملامسة حقيقة في تماس البدنين بشئ من أجزائهما من غير تقييد باليد

rows.speaker: الجلال المحلي والكمال ابن أبي شريف
rows.claim: Al-Jalal al-Mahalli calls touching by hand literal; Ibn Abi Sharif says this exemplifies one kind of touch rather than defining the full literal meaning.
rows.anchor: وادعى الجلال المحلى أن الملامسة حقيقة في الجس باليد تمثيلا للملامسة بنوع من أنواعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bodily events trigger purification; lack of water or ability to use it is the actual condition licensing tayammum.
rows.anchor: ليس باعتبار أنفسهما بل باعتبار قيدهما المستفاد من قوله سبحانه : فلم تجدوا ماء بل هو السبب في الحقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The events prepare for the water condition and show that it licenses relief after the cause of purification arises for either minor or major impurity.
rows.anchor: وإنما ذكرا تمهيدا له وتنبيها على أنه سبب للرخصة بعد انعقاد سبب الطهارة بقسميها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One explanation says water absence also conditions illness and travel, but need not be repeated because major impurity is already clear there and minor impurity follows by textual implication.
rows.anchor: قيل : وتخصيص ذكره بهذه الصورة مع أنه معتبر أيضا في صورة المرض والسفر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A view makes lack of water a condition applying to all, including the purification implied by the two bodily-event clauses; al-Alusi says the syntax does not support it.
rows.anchor: إن هذا القيد راجع للكل وقيد وجوب التطهر المكنى عنه بالمجئ من الغائط

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: A proposal reorders the verse: prohibit prayer in intoxication, janaba, or after either event, then command tayammum for illness or travel; al-Alusi objects that it splits condition and result without rationale.
rows.anchor: وفي الكشف عن بعضهم أن في الآية تقديما وتأخيرا والتقدير لا تقربوا الصلاة وأنتم سكارى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi prefers the apparent order: waterlessness can mean inability to use water and govern all cases, or retain its literal sense without attaching it to illness and travel.
rows.anchor: ولعل الأوجه في تقرير الآية والله تعالى أعلم أن يجعل عدم الوجدان عبارة عن عدم القدرة على استعمال الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Illness and travel need not be restricted to people already in minor or major impurity: the verse explains the switch from water purification to tayammum.
rows.anchor: وأن يبقى قوله سبحانه : ( مرضى أو على سفر ) على إطلاقه من غير تقييد بكونهم محدثين أو مجنبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People outside illness and travel illustrate that inability to use water for other reasons also licenses tayammum; the ritual event itself is not the cause.
rows.anchor: وأن يجعل ذكر المحدثين من غير القبيلين بيانا لسبب العدول وهو فقد القدرة من غير سفر ولا مرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naming the events before waterlessness signals that lack of water licenses relief only after purification becomes obligatory.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل أو لم تجدوا دون ذكر السببين تنبيها على أن عدم الوجدان مرخص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first fa coordinates; the fa in the tayammum command answers the whole condition, whose pronoun covers all cases, so no separate command for the latrine clause is needed.
rows.anchor: والفاء في ( فلم ) عاطفة وأما الفاء في قوله سبحانه : ( فتيمموا صعيدا طيبا فواقعة في جواب الشرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tayammum literally means intending; al-Aʿsha's line illustrates the sense.
rows.anchor: والتيمم لغة القصد قال الأعشى : ( تيممت قيسا )

rows.speaker: الخليل وثعلب
rows.claim: Al-Khalil and Thaʿlab define ṣaʿīd as the earth's surface; al-Zajjaj says linguists do not disagree.
rows.anchor: والصعيد وجه الأرض كما روي عن الخليل وثعلب وقال الزجاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣaʿīd may mean the furthest surface reached from the earth's interior or what is raised above the earth.
rows.anchor: وسمي بذلك لأنه نهاية ما يصعد إليه من باطن الأرض

rows.speaker: سفيان
rows.claim: Sufyan glosses ṭayyib as lawful; another sense is plant-growing rather than saline, as in 7:58.
rows.anchor: وعن سفيان الحلال وقيل : المنبت دون السبخة كما في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sense pure best fits purification: aim for a clean part of the earth's surface.
rows.anchor: والحمل على الأول هو الأنسب بمقام الطهارة والمعنى فتعمدوا واقصدوا شيئا من وجه الأرض طاهرا

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة ومحمد
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa and one report from Muhammad permit tayammum with kohl, brick, litharge, gems, or coral without dust.
rows.anchor: وهذا دليل واضح لجواز التيمم بالكحل والآجر والمرداسنج والياقوت

rows.speaker: محمد وأبو يوسف والشافعي وأحمد
rows.claim: Another report from Muhammad, with Abu Yusuf, al-Shafiʿi, and Ahmad, requires dust to adhere, citing the partitive من in 5:6; Hanafis read it as origination or customary wording.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية أخرى عنه وهو قول أبي يوسف والشافعي وأحمد رضي الله تعالى عنهم أنه لا يجوز التيمم إلا أن يعلق باليد

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik permits tayammum with snow; al-Alusi notes Shiite criticism and says he defended Malik in a separate work.
rows.anchor: وأغرب الإمام مالك فأجاز التيمم بالثلج وقد شنع الشيعة عليه بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣaʿīdan is a direct object, or is accusative after an omitted preposition meaning “with a surface.”
rows.anchor: ونصب ( صعيدا ) على أنه مفعول به وقيل : إنه منصوب بنزع الخافض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ is connective; the apparent ruling requires wiping the whole face and hands, so leaving any part unwiped invalidates tayammum.
rows.anchor: أي وجوهكم وأيديكم على أن الباء صلة والمراد استيعاب هذين العضوين بالمسح

rows.speaker: الحسن عن الإمام
rows.claim: A report from Hasan on Abu Hanifa's authority says wiping most of each area suffices, as full coverage is not required for wiping boots or head.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية الحسن عن الإمام رضي الله تعالى عنه أن الأكثر يقوم مقام الكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi prefers full coverage because tayammum substitutes for ablution, which requires it; fingers are separated and rings removed.
rows.anchor: ووجه الظاهر أن التيمم قائم مقام الوضوء ولهذا قالوا : يخلل الأصابع وينزع الخاتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yad can cover the hand through the wrist, elbow, or armpit; treating these ranges as literal explains early disagreement.
rows.anchor: وأيدي جمع يد وهي مشتركة بين معان من أطراف الأصابع إلى الرسغ وإلى المرفق

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari transmits al-Zuhri's view that tayammum wiping reaches the armpits.
rows.anchor: فأخرج ابن جرير عن الزهري أن التيمم إلى الآباط

rows.speaker: مكحول
rows.claim: Al-Tabari transmits Makḥul's view of a strike for the face and palms through the wrists.
rows.anchor: وأخرج عن مكحول أنه قال : التيمم ضربة للوجه والكفين إلى الكوع

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Al-Hakim reports from Ibn ʿUmar that they wiped from elbows to palms over the hair-bearing areas on both sides.
rows.anchor: وأخرج الحاكم عن ابن عمر في كيفية تيممهم مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو داود
rows.claim: A report in Abu Dawud says the Prophet wiped his hands to the elbows; al-Alusi identifies this as his school's, al-Shafiʿi's, and most scholars' view.
rows.anchor: ومن حديث أبي داود أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم تيمم ومسح يديه إلى مرفقيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wiping to the elbows is supported by analogy with ablution, the original purification; the majority also report its validity.
rows.anchor: ويشهد لهم القياس على الوضوء الذي هو أصله وإن كان الحدث والجنابة فيه كيفية سواء

rows.speaker: عمر وابن عمر وابن مسعود
rows.claim: Reports from ʿUmar, Ibn ʿUmar, and Ibn Masʿud deny tayammum for janaba, menstruation, and postpartum impurity; they regard it as a nonanalogical concession for minor impurity only.
rows.anchor: ومن الناس من قال : لا يتيمم الجنب والحائض والنفساء وهو المروي عن عمر وابنه وابن مسعود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi says the verse is nearly explicit that a person in janaba may use tayammum, even if touching women is not read as intercourse; hadith reports confirm this.
rows.anchor: وأنت تعلم أن الآية كالصريح في جواز تيمم الجنب وإن لم تحمل الملامسة على الوقاع

rows.speaker: عمران بن حصين
rows.claim: In a Bukhari report from ʿImran ibn Husayn, a man says he is in janaba without water, and the Prophet tells him to use earth, which suffices.
rows.anchor: أخرج البخاري عن عمران بن حصين أن رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم رأى رجلا معتزلا

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: People in sandy country with no water for a month or two, including people in janaba, menstruation, and postpartum impurity, are told by the Prophet to use their land.
rows.anchor: وروي أن قوما جاءوا إلى رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم وقالوا : إنا قوم نسكن هذه الرمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars disagree whether tayammum removes ritual impurity; on close inspection this verse proves neither position.
rows.anchor: وهل يرفع التيمم الحدث أم لا خلاف ولا دلالة في الآية على أحد الأمرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The divine names explain and affirm the dispensation: God's settled practice is to pardon those at fault and forgive sinners, so He provides ease.
rows.anchor: تعليل لما يفهمه الكلام من الترخيص والتيسير وتقرير لهما فإن من عادته المستمرة أن يعفو

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes ʿafw here to mean facilitation, citing the Prophet's statement that he waived alms on horses and slaves.
rows.anchor: وقيل : العفو هنا بمعنى التيسير كما في التيسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi says the facilitation sense in the hadith is not certain, and it is unlikely that forgiveness here specifically concerns those who prayed intoxicated and their recitation.
rows.anchor: وأنت تعلم أن حمل العفو على التيسير في الحديث غير متعين وكون ذكر المغفرة لما ذكر بعيد

words: أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ يُزَكُّونَ أَنفُسَهُم
rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says the verse concerns Jews who brought their children to the Prophet, asked whether the children sinned, then claimed their day and night sins were alternately erased.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي : نزلت في رجال من اليهود أتوا رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم بأطفالهم

words: أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ يُزَكُّونَ أَنفُسَهُم
rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Tabari reports al-Hasan's view that Jews and Christians claimed to be God's children and beloved and that only their communities would enter Paradise.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير عن الحسن أنها نزلت في اليهود والنصارى حيث قالوا

words: أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ يُزَكُّونَ أَنفُسَهُم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address bids the listener wonder at their claim to purity despite disbelief and grave sin, or their claim that God erases their day and night sins.
rows.anchor: والمعنى انظر إليهم وتعجب من ادعائهم أنهم أزكياء عند الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The criticism also applies to anyone praising himself without sound purpose, apart from legitimate mention of God's favor.
rows.anchor: وفي معناهم من زكى نفسه وأثنى عليها لغير غرض صحيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause overturns their self-purification and affirms God's purification of deserving believers; it does not pivot to a charge of miserliness and envy.
rows.anchor: إبطال لتزكية أنفسهم وإثبات لتزكية الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause is coordinated with an implied statement: they do not truly purify themselves; rather, God purifies deserving servants.
rows.anchor: والجملة عطف على مقدر ينساق إليه الكلام كأنه قيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tazkiya means purification and removal of what is blameworthy, as in 91:9 and 9:103.
rows.anchor: وأصل التزكية التطهير والتنزيه من القبيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fatil is the thread in the cleft of a date stone, an image for the tiniest amount, like naqir and qitmir.
rows.anchor: وهو المراد بالفتيل وهو الخيط الذي في شق النواة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وأبو مالك والسدي
rows.claim: Another gloss says fatil is grime that comes out between one's fingers and palm, attributed to Ibn ʿAbbas, Abu Malik, and al-Suddi.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الفتيل ما خرج بين إصبعيك وكفيك من الوسخ وروي ذلك عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause attaches to an omitted statement: they will be punished for the heinous claim without even the slightest injustice.
rows.anchor: أي يعاقبون بتلك الفعلة الشنيعة ولا يظلمون في ذلك العقاب أدنى ظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the clause is circumstantial, with its pronoun referring by sense to those God purifies: they receive their full reward at the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن تكون جملة ( ولا يظلمون ) في موضع الحال والضمير راجع إلى من

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view makes the clause independent and its pronoun refer to both self-purifiers and those God purifies; neither group's punishment or reward is reduced. Al-Alusi prefers the first reading in the warning context.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو استئناف والضمير عائد على الموصولين من زكى نفسه ومن زكاه الله تعالى

rows.speaker: علي بن عيسى
rows.claim: Fatil is accusative as a second object of “wronged”; ʿAli ibn ʿIsa also allows an accusative of specification, like “I sweated sweat.”
rows.anchor: قال علي بن عيسى : ويحتمل أن يكون تمييزا كقولك تصببت عرقا

words: أَنظُرْ كَيْفَ يَفْتَرُونَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ ٱلْكَذِبَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their lie is the claim that God deems them pure, accepts them, and chooses them; “look how” intensifies denunciation and wonder, while they also lie about themselves.
rows.anchor: في زعمهم أنهم أزكياء عند الله تعالى المتضمن لزعمهم قبول الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: How is accusative, analyzed as adverbial or circumstantial under the disagreement between Sibawayh and al-Akhfash; Abu al-Baqa makes it a state of the lie.
rows.anchor: و ( كيف ) في موضع نصب إما على التشبيه بالظرف أو بالحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explicit word lie intensifies condemnation, although fabrication already entails falsehood.
rows.anchor: والتصريح بالكذب مع أن الافتراء لا يكون إلا كذبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sufficient manifest sin is their fabrication, or this particular lie; a person openly committing such sin cannot be God's child, beloved, or pure.
rows.anchor: أي بافترائهم وقيل : بهذا الكذب الخاص

rows.speaker: عصام الملة
rows.claim: ʿIsam al-Milla analyzes the clause as circumstantial with an implied قد; ithman is accusative as specification.
rows.anchor: كما قال عصام الملة : في موضع الحال بتقدير قد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse resumes the preceding discussion as explanation: its referent is either those rejecting Muhammad or everyone rejecting any prophet, and the signs then include all prophetic proofs.
rows.anchor: استنئاف وقع كالبيان والتقرير لما قبله

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh says sawfa signals threat and warning, with the shorter sa serving similarly, as in 74:26.
rows.anchor: كما قال سيبويه : كلمة تذكر للتهديد والوعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sawfa and sa can also promise good, as in 93:5 and 12:98, though they often intensify a threat.
rows.anchor: وقد تذكر للوعد كما في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite fire magnifies it: they will certainly enter a formidable fire.
rows.anchor: وتنكير ( نارا ) للتفخيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nadhijat means the skins are thoroughly cooked, consumed, and disintegrated, by analogy with ripened fruit or meat.
rows.anchor: من نضج الثمر واللحم نضجا ونضجا إذا أدرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kullama is a temporal adverb governed by baddalnahum: at each skin's burning, God gives another skin in its place.
rows.anchor: و ( كلما ) ظرف زمان والعامل فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection that the replacement skin did not sin mistakes the skin for the responsible subject: skin lacks perception and agency, like an instrument such as a killer's hand or sword.
rows.anchor: وذلك لأنه هو العاصى باعتبار أصله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pain and reward belong to the sentient soul in whatever body it inhabits; bodily parts change during life, so continuity need not mean identical matter.
rows.anchor: فالحق أن العذاب على النفس الحساسة بأي بدن حلت وفي أي جلد كانت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The enormous bodies described for Hell and Paradise show that people need not perform worldly deeds with precisely those bodies; an iron body example also defeats the objection.
rows.anchor: وأن سن الجهنمي كجبل أحد وأن أهل الجنة يدخلونها على طول آدم عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If bodily resurrection were not established as necessary religious doctrine, purely spiritual reward and punishment would not be rationally implausible.
rows.anchor: ولولا ما علم من الدين بالضرورة من المعاد الجسماني بحيث صار إنكاره كفرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi does not deny that annihilated bodies can be recreated; he says re-creation is unnecessary though possible, and either identity or similar-body accounts preserve bodily resurrection.
rows.anchor: ولا يتوهم من هذا إني أقول باستحالة إعادة المعدوم معاذ الله تعالى ولكني أقول بعدم الحاجة إلى إعادته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scriptural evidence differs between restoring the same bodies after annihilation and creating similar bodies while the first perish; either can be accepted with bodily resurrection.
rows.anchor: فمنها ما يدل على إعادة الأجسام بعينها بعد إعدامها ومنها ما يدل على خلق مثلها وفناء الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi says he will later discuss texts that appear to show bodily identity, including tongues, hands, and feet testifying in 24:24.
rows.anchor: مثل قوله سبحانه : ( يوم تشهد عليهم ألسنتهم وأيديهم وأرجلهم بما كانوا يعملون )

rows.speaker: السفيري
rows.claim: Al-Safiri's commentary reports the soul and body blaming each other, with an angel comparing them to a seeing cripple and blind man who jointly take fruit; al-Alusi rejects the analogy because the bodily instrument lacks choice and awareness.
rows.anchor: وما في شرح البخاري للسفيري من أنه لا تزال الخصومة بين الناس حتى تختصم الروح والجسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The soul-body garden parable fails because the bodily instrument has no choice or awareness; only an unknown form of consciousness could alter the comparison.
rows.anchor: لظهور الفرق بين المثال والممثل له فإن الحامل فيما نحن فيه لا اختيار له ولا شعور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The skin replacement can occur many times in one hour.
rows.anchor: ثم إن هذا التبديل كيفما كان يكون في الساعة الواحدة مرات كثيرة

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Mardawayh and Abu Nuʿaym report from Ibn ʿUmar that Kaʿb explained skins are replaced 120 times in an hour and ʿUmar affirmed hearing this from the Prophet.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال : قرئ عند عمر هذه الآية فقال كعب : عندي تفسيرها

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Shayba and others report from al-Hasan that the fire consumes a person's flesh 70,000 times daily, each time telling them to return.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن قال : بلغني أنه يحرق أحدهم في اليوم سبعين ألف مرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Taste the punishment” means experience continues without interruption; tasting also conveys bitterness, acute impact, and inward penetration.
rows.anchor: أي ليدوم ذوقه ولا ينقطع كقولك للعزيز : أعزك الله

rows.speaker: شيخ الإسلام
rows.claim: A wisdom for changing skins is to prevent souls from imagining that perception ends in burning or that pain may be spared as the body is spared burning.
rows.anchor: قاله مولانا شيخ الإسلام

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another proposed wisdom is that renewal creates despair and grief upon grief.
rows.anchor: وقيل : السر في ذلك أن في النضج والتبديل نوع إياس لهم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some deny literal burning and replacement of skins, claiming the replacement refers to garments in 14:50 called skins by proximity; al-Alusi rejects this as departing from the plain sense.
rows.anchor: وأنكر بعضهم نضج الجلود بالمعنى المتبادر وتبديلها زاعما أن التبديل إنما هو للسرابيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The garment reading is an unwarranted departure from the plain text and established teaching; literal skin replacement is within God's power.
rows.anchor: وفيه أنه ترك للظاهر ويوشك أن يكون خلاف المعلوم ضرورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAziz means ever invincible, unopposed and unprevented.
rows.anchor: عزيزا أي لم يزل منيعا لا يدافع ولا يمانع

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation takes ʿaziz to mean capable of carrying out whatever God threatens or promises.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إنه قادر لا يمتنع عليه ما يريده مما تواعد أو وعد به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hakim describes God's governance, decree, and punishment; the clause explains the preceding casting into fire and skin replacement, with the divine name emphasized to ground the ruling.
rows.anchor: في تدبيره وتقديره وتعذيب من يعذبه والجملة تعليل لما قبلها من الإصلاء والتبديل
